caption:
Claude Code is halfway through a refactor. You have a question. So you interrupt it, and now it is answering you instead of working.

There is a command that fixes this and almost nobody uses it.

/btw. As in, by the way.

Type /btw followed by your question. The answer comes back in an overlay you dismiss with Escape. Three things happen, and all three matter.

The task never stops. It is single turn and it runs while the main work keeps going.

The question never enters your conversation history. Neither does the answer. Your context stays clean.

And it has no tools. It only knows what is already in the session. So ask it about work Claude has already seen, not about something it would have to go and find.

If the answer turns out to need real work, press f. It forks the question and the answer into a background subagent that does have tools.

Every detail here is from Anthropic's own docs and the Claude Code power user tips page.

Now the part that is not about code.

The habit worth stealing is this one: do not stop something that is already running to ask it a question. Most businesses do the opposite. They pause the campaign to check the campaign. They stop the machine, look inside, and call the pause "being careful".

The teams that grow build a side channel instead. Questions go to the side. The work stays on the rails.
